research_rationale: EO 8718 establishes the Subic Bay Naval Defensive Sea Area and Subic Bay Naval Airspace Reservation in the Philippine Islands. EO 9720, signed May 8, 1946 and published May 10, 1946 (11 FR 5105), discontinues both the airspace reservation and the defensive sea area by naming EO 8718 for each, so every clause ends on May 8, 1946. The order states no separate effective date for 9720, so its signature date is recorded. The OFR-catalog hit for this order is the cross-reference from EO 9720; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit. The order's own effective-date sentence (ninety days after March 22, 1941) is part of the final clause. Quotations are single lines of the OCR text layer.
savings_reason: The order states that violations of its provisions are punishable under section 44 of the Criminal Code and the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938. Liability for violations committed while the areas were in force rests on those statutes, not on a continuing command of the order; EO 9720 discontinues the areas and contains no sentence about past violations. No command of EO 8718 survives May 8, 1946.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end found: the OFR edge and my scan of held texts for "Subic Bay Naval" and "No. 8718" (cruden.py, 2026-11-04) show only EO 9720 as an instrument discontinuing the areas; later orders printed beside EO 8718 in the 1941 issue merely repeat the penalty wording for their own areas.

The enforcement span includes table-of-contents text that the OCR layer interleaves in the middle of that sentence.
independent_command_check: Each clause concerns only the Subic Bay areas and each is discontinued with them by EO 9720; none rests on an authority outside the order that would survive the discontinuance.
savings_check: EO 9720 has no savings clause; accrued statutory liability for past violations is the only residual effect and is stated to rest on the statutes.
